Beat Press
One ball, one press, one beat. Metal arms, pistons or an iris gate shut on every hit of the music, and each press multiplies the balls and gives them a new colour, until thousands fill the arena on the last drop. The track is written by the game for every video (808 phonk), or the presses can play a song from its MIDI notes.

Which formula grows faster? Every tower has one: n³ against n!, 2ⁿ against 10n², any pair you like. In a real 3D scene the balls of each tower smash their way down through glass platforms, or the towers fill up with blocks to a goal line, and level after level the formulas decide how many balls there are and how hard they hit.

Tipping Point
One small hero and one number. Little helpers walk in from both sides and multiply it, the weather takes from it and knocks the helpers out. The number sinks, hovers, gets a false hope or two, and then the growth runs away to 99,999,999 and the hero fills the frame. Seven scenes (campfire, snow cabin, desert sprout, snowman, lighthouse, city power, cloud), four rule sets including a duel, and four endings.

Ricochet Rally
Squares ricochet through a board of rooms and corridors while a flood sweeps in behind them. Stripes give way after a few knocks, numbered blocks lose one with every hit, and in the squeeze between flood and gate the hits turn into a rattle until the gate gives way. Race to the checkered line or fight for the knife: the last square standing wins. Six seeded boards, six kinds of gates, spikes, skull tiles, boost pads, cloning apples, your own photos on the squares.

Spiral Shatter
A ball is thrown into a spiral full of glass. It smashes its way round until its energy is gone, the glass grows back, and the next try starts with one thing changed: the shape, the object, the speed, the size or the glass. The last try always reaches the centre and sets off the finale. Six kinds of glass, five series, nine palettes and four endings.

Ribbon Fold
A real 3D ribbon folds on a plate: every fold copies the whole ribbon, lifts the copy and swings it about the end, so the pieces double (2, 4, 8 ... 4,096) while the camera pulls back. Will it fit? At the end more ribbons turn in around the start without a single overlap, a wave runs along it, or it folds back into one strip. Glossy plastic, chrome, neon, glass or pearl on nine stages, with a rising note for every fold.

Fold Groove
A paper strip that folds to the beat. The game writes its own 808 track for every video, and every bass hit copies the strip and swings the copy open, doubling it into dragon-curve lace. Fills fold it back, every drop slams a new shape in, and the last hit spins the figure into a pinwheel. Flat paper-cut, poster, retro, ink and chalk looks.

Fold Fractal
Fold a glowing strip in half again and again and open every crease to the same angle: each fold copies the whole line and swings the copy about its end, so the layers double until a dragon curve appears. Start from a strip, a T, a wave or a lightning bolt, fold at 90, 108 or 120 degrees, left or right, up to 26 times, then let two or four dragons meet at one corner, fill the screen, or unfold it all again. Every fold plays the next note of a rising scale.

A song played on staircases: every voice gets its own stairs, every note is a step, and a ball lands on it exactly when the note sounds. Long notes are long steps, quick runs are tiny ones, and a voice that pauses goes dark until it joins in again. Pick a public-domain classic, an original or a polyrhythm, or load your own MIDI file.

Hive Burst
A wall of small glass tiles, coloured in rings, with one ball in a hole in the middle. A tile cracks on the first touch and breaks on the second, and every broken tile frees another ball, so the hole grows into a glowing wave until the whole frame is bouncing balls. Chain reactions, colour bursts, a colour race, six tile shapes, fifteen colour patterns including your own word, six boards, gravity and six sound sets.

Sync Fountain
A polyrhythm you can watch. Glowing balls ride arcs, hop out of a fountain, bounce in glass pipes, drip onto tuned wine glasses or swing as metronomes, and each one rings a note at the moment it touches. Every ball makes a whole number of trips per loop, so the pattern drifts apart and lines up again exactly at the end: a perfect loop.

A pendulum wave of glowing dots. Each dot runs its own closed path a different whole number of times per loop and rings a chime when it passes the trigger, so one neat line unfolds into spirals and rosettes and then lines up again exactly. Eleven path families, ten looks and six instrument kits; every clip is a perfect loop.

Star Beats
A ball bounces inside a ring and draws a new star every bar. Every bounce is a note that lands exactly on the beat, every star ends on a chord, and layer by layer the bounces grow from single hits into a full track. Also a climb to bigger and bigger stars, a choir of balls that builds one chord, and a band where every ball is an instrument. Original synthesized sound; tempo, key, chords, instruments, arenas and looks are adjustable.

Every Bounce
A ball or a block bounces inside an outlined arena and leaves a copy of itself on every frame, so its whole path stays on screen as a rainbow ribbon. Every bounce changes it: bigger, faster, both or smaller, until it fills the arena or the picture breaks into loose stamps. Also a black hole that keeps pulling harder, two to four shapes that collide, seven shapes, seven arenas, ten looks, a tune played by the bounces.

Digit Duel
Balls duel with maths. Each ball bounces in its own box on a stack of health layers (1.000, 10.000.000.000, 1.000.000.000.000.000) and every touch takes its damage off the top one. The damage follows the ball's rule: Fibonacci, factorial, doubling, primes, digits of pi, dice, speed, gravity, grow, split, laser or bomb. First through every layer wins. Duel, 4-way race, tournament match with bracket, or a full 4-ball cup.

Wobble Stack
Soft falling blocks in a real 3D cabinet. Tetris-style pieces drop one by one, land crooked, bounce, lean on each other and wobble into the wall by themselves: every move is simulated soft-body physics. Then a press squashes the pile until the blocks burst out onto the floor. Pick jelly, fur, steel or a mix of materials, each with its own physics and sound. Switch on line clears, change the scene, the pieces, the camera and the ending, and put your own text on the engraved sign.
